title: VGA: Hardware Accelerator for Scalable Long Sequence Model Inference
problem: Self-attention transformers have quadratic complexity in sequence length, and state space models using FFT-based convolution suffer from extremely low compute utilization and memory bandwidth bottlenecks on data-parallel accelerators like GPUs.
motivation: Long sequence modeling is critical for modern applications, but current hardware-algorithm mismatches waste significant compute and energy on GPUs.
method: VGA introduces Complex number Compute Units (CCUs) that fully utilize on-chip SRAM bandwidth for FFT-based convolution. Parameters are generated on-the-fly to minimize required SRAM capacity. The architecture is specifically optimized to execute global convolution operators from SSM-based models like H3 with high throughput.
key_novelty: Custom Complex number Compute Units combined with on-the-fly parameter generation to eliminate memory bandwidth bottlenecks in FFT-based global convolution.
contributions: Hardware accelerator architecture optimized for FFT-based global convolution in SSM models
Complex number Compute Units design for maximizing SRAM bandwidth utilization
On-the-fly parameter generation to reduce SRAM capacity requirements
76× area efficiency and 48× power efficiency improvements over NVIDIA A100
primary_theme: Custom accelerator for efficient FFT-based global convolution
